Nothing in the engine or the specs records, per finding, whether the visit it started built or refused it. The engine gives only a visit-level blocker. I did not open the judge spec's omitted line 80 or the visit state at `nodes.py:565`/`:1689`, so the visit-level outcome is inferred.

ARTIFACT gap_finding: RRN-B14 (`plugins/tempergraph/docs/specs/reruns-and-feedback.spec.md:21-25`) says that on `back:<unit>` or `rewind:<unit>`, feedback becomes that unit's visit reason and its judge gets "an engine blocker that every point is addressed". It is the only per-visit result, and it says nothing per finding. `judging.py:176-178` (read) gives the judge a visit reason with one extra blocker, "every point of this reason is addressed", and no per-point id. `nodes.py:565` (first attempt only) and `nodes.py:1689` (read) take the reason from `state["visits"][unit]["reason"]`. `judging.py:165-172` handles feedback and rulings separately, and `judging.py:169-171` adds a `ruling` blocker whose unmet case is `no_change`. The ruling ADR `feedback-can-be-a-lasting-ruling.adr.md:38` (A1) says a blocker against a ruling escalates. `test_feedback.py:1,96` covers feedback and refusals, and I found no test of a per-finding result. Searched: "addressed", "every point", "visit_reason", RRN-B14 in `plugins/`. I found no per-finding "built or refused" record, so the new unit spec would define it as a reading of the visit's verdict: the visit-reason blocker passes or fails as a whole. Unconfirmed: whether the verdict shows which point failed (see `judge-and-verdict.spec.md:80`, not read).
